title: Stream epoch negotiation and loss-tolerance for SSE streaming
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Clients currently rely solely on resume tokens that are brittle across model variants and transient socket failure patterns. When reconnects happen we see duplicate function-call events, truncated structured outputs, and occasional long tail of replays that confuse downstream consumers (console, SDKs, downstream caches).

Goal: Design and implement an "epoch negotiation" layer and loss-tolerance heuristics on the server-side SSE implementation to make reconnect behavior idempotent, bounded, and compatible with older clients. The implementation should preserve tool/function-call atomicity and ensure structured outputs (JSON/JSONL/function calls) are reconstructed reliably on reconnect without requiring changes to most clients.

Scope: protocol design, server runtime changes (token generation and validation), SDK shim compatibility, telemetry/instrumentation, and a staged rollout with feature-flag gating. Not in scope: reworking model generation semantics or client-side offline stitching (clients may still opt into advanced SDK helpers).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits an epoch token tied to a short-lived write epoch for every SSE session and returns a resumable offset (epoch_id + seq) in every chunk header

On reconnect, server will accept resume requests that provide a last-known (epoch_id, seq) and either resume from the same epoch or perform a bounded graft from a compatible epoch variant within a configurable staleness window
Function-call boundaries are preserved: no duplicate function-call invocation events are delivered to the same logical session after a successful resume

Legacy clients that only send resume_token continue to work: server maps legacy resume_token to the most recently active epoch if within staleness window, otherwise falls back to restarting the session cleanly
End-to-end tests cover: duplicate chunk suppression, soft-merge of partially overlapping fragments, strong-merge when epochs are identical, and graceful restart when epochs are incompatible
Telemetry emits: resume_attempt, resume_success, resume_fallback, duplicate_chunk_detected, epoch_graft_performed with contextual labels (model_variant, region, client_sdk_version)
Rollout gated behind feature flag with a canary that starts at 1% of sessions and scales to 100% with automated rollback on error-rate regressions
Documentation updated (Console: streaming semantics, SDK: recommended resume usage) and a single GitHub PR links to the runtime changes
implementation_notes:
Design summary: introduce a short epoch token (uuid-ish) generated at session start that is monotonically increasing per model variant/route. Each SSE chunk header will include: epoch_id, chunk_seq (int), optionally chunk_hash and last_stable_seq. Chunks remain JSONL payloads with an outer metadata envelope to remain compatible with existing clients that expect text/event-stream.

Key heuristics:
- Soft-merge mode: when reconnecting to a different epoch that is newer but within a configurable staleness window (default 20s / 50 chunks), attempt to graft overlapping output by comparing chunk_hashes and seq ranges to avoid re-sending already delivered tokens.
- Strong-merge mode: if epoch_id matches, perform idempotent fast-replay: accept resume_seq and continue emitting next_seq = resume_seq+1.
- Fallback restart: if epochs are incompatible (staleness exceeded or variant mismatch), close prior session gap and start a fresh session with explicit restart event so SDKs/console can surface a clean boundary.

Function-call preservation: function-call events must include call_id and finality marker (call_end). Resume logic must treat call_id as atomic; if a call_end exists before resume_seq, do not re-emit the call. If call_end falls after resume_seq, server will re-emit remaining fragments and a call_end when completed.

Backward compatibility: older clients may not parse epoch headers. To preserve compatibility, the server will continue emitting canonical SSE lines for legacy flows and will accept legacy resume_token values that map to the current epoch via a short-lived index table. The index table purges entries after staleness_window.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag the epoch negotiation on the runtime config, default OFF
QA + internal canary: enable for internal infra and staging (end-to-end SDKs + console playback)
Canary 1% production for low-risk routes (embeddings/low-throughput chat) for 48 hours
Expand to 10% and monitor duplicate_chunk_detected and resume_fallback metrics for 72 hours
If stable, expand to 50% then 100% over 7 days
If any rollback criteria triggered (resume_failure_rate > 0.5% above baseline OR client-visible duplicates > 0.2%), auto-revert to previous flag state and open incident runbook
test_plan: Unit tests for header encoding/decoding (epoch_id + seq + optional hash)
Integration harness: simulated flaky networks that drop TCP mid-chunk and rejoin with various resume payloads
SDK compatibility tests: legacy SDK (v1.3) + new SDK (v2.0) against canary runtime asserting behavior matches compatibility matrix
Chaos test: orchestrate rapid reconnect storms from multiple regions and assert telemetry counters and no functional duplicates for function-call boundaries
Load test: ensure added epoch index/table lookups do not increase p95 response time by >5% under production load
metrics: resume_success: resumes that replayed without restart
resume_fallback: resumes that resulted in restart
duplicate_chunk_detected: server-detected duplicate chunk at resume time
p95_reconnect_latency: end-to-end time to first token after reconnect
comments: 2026-02-25 Liam Chen: Initial ticket created after incident INC-2026-02-21 where two shoppers saw duplicate tool calls after reconnect. Captured preliminary design in Confluence.
2026-02-28 Marina Ortega: Spike results uploaded — epoch token generation adds ~0.8ms p50 to chunk emit path using a small in-memory epoch cache. Need to explore off-heap caching for p95 safety.

2026-03-03 Devin Park (runtime): Prototype implemented; basic resume success flow verified locally. Observed edge-case when chunk_hash collisions occur across rapid model rollouts — added sequence disambiguation to spec.
2026-03-05 Design review (Aisha Thompson): UX note — console should show a ‘resumed’ badge with resume_reason (same_epoch | grafted | restarted). Avoid exposing raw tokens to end users.
2026-03-08 QA: Integration tests failing intermittently for legacy-mapping TTL expiry. Reduced TTL from 60s to 30s and added telemetry to monitor mapping_miss_count.
